name: Malformation of the Neurenteric Canal, Spinal Cord and Column

criteria.description: Identification of neurenteric cyst or canal malformation on spinal imaging
Presence of associated spinal cord anomalies such as tethered cord or syringomyelia
Congenital vertebral column malformations including hemivertebrae or segmentation defects
Neurological deficits consistent with spinal cord involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of neurenteric cyst or canal malformation on imaging plus at least one associated spinal cord or vertebral malformation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging findings combined with clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neurenteric cyst detected on spinal MRI
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic cystic lesion along the spinal canal

searchTerms: birth defects in spine bone segments
abnormal sensations in feet and legs

common.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction including urinary retention or incontinence
searchTerms: bladder problems like retention or leakage

occasional.symptomName: Back pain localized to spinal deformity

searchTerms: increased muscle tone in lower limbs

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to neurenteric cyst expansion
searchTerms: brain fluid buildup from spinal cyst growth
hydrocephalus caused by expanding spinal cyst
fluid pressure in brain due to cyst

rare.symptomName: Respiratory compromise due to high cervical spinal involvement
searchTerms: breathing problems from high neck spine issues
respiratory difficulty due to cervical spine damage
breathing compromise from upper spine involvement
cutaneous signs on back over spine malformation

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine labs typically normal
imaging: MRI showing neurenteric cyst along spinal canal
CT or X-ray demonstrating vertebral segmentation anomalies
Possible syringomyelia or tethered cord on spinal MRI
genetic: No well-defined genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Neurological examination revealing motor and sensory deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of open neural tube defect
Distinct cutaneous markers such as myelomeningocele
Arachnoid cysts lack epithelial lining characteristic of neurenteric cysts
